title: ServiceNow Pricing 2026: Per-Seat Costs and Add-Ons
summary: ServiceNow pricing varies by plan and licenses, with costs often lower than list rates. Understand the pricing factors and how to get accurate quotes.
body_markdown:
## Automate around ServiceNow with Activepieces


If your extra workflows are mostly ticket, chat, form and spreadsheet glue, Activepieces, which MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run in production, can run them outside ServiceNow, so they stop adding to your module and seat count.


### Where a separate workflow tool saves licence spend


Activepieces is a workflow builder, not an ITSM platform.


Its value here is narrow: routine automations such as copying new requests into a tracking sheet, posting an approval prompt in chat, or turning a form submission into a record don't need a priced ServiceNow add-on or extra integration capacity, and since every Activepieces plan, including free, allows unlimited flows, one more of them doesn't add a licence line.


### What the workflow builder shows


The flow builder below shows the pattern. A Schedule trigger set to "Every Hour" is selected, the integration picker offers spreadsheet apps with actions like Insert Row and Find Rows, and the settings panel shows a successful sample-data test.


Hourly polling means a change can reach the sheet up to an hour late, so this suits reporting and housekeeping, not anything an agent is waiting on.


The test result matters more than the picker. You can see what the trigger returns before wiring anything downstream, which is how you find out early whether a flow carries the fields you need.


The same canvas works for any app in the catalogue, so one tool covers several small jobs instead of a licence line for each.


### What it costs and what it connects to


Activepieces' pricing page lists the Free plan at $0 with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it contains, so a ten-step flow costs the same as a two-step one.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so the same ten-step flow is metered step by step there.


The core is MIT-licensed, with the enterprise directories under a separate commercial licence in the repository's LICENSE file, and the 746 integrations are counted from the packages/integrations/community directory of its open source monorepo. The free Community Edition can be self-hosted.


The saving only exists if that cost sits below the ServiceNow quote line it replaces.


Check the ServiceNow integration's documentation for which actions it exposes, since a connector that only reads records saves less than one that creates and updates them.


### Where it does not replace ServiceNow


It's the wrong choice when the process is the system of record. Incident, change and approval workflows that auditors inspect, and anything tied to ServiceNow's data model, access controls or fulfiller roles, belong inside the platform.


Moving them out leaves you with two places to reconcile and a second tool holding credentials to the first.


It's also the wrong choice when the person doing the work needs to be in ServiceNow anyway. Automation outside it doesn't remove a fulfiller seat for someone who works tickets all day. It only removes the cost of automating around those people.


Budget it as a side tool for low-risk glue, not as an exit from the quote.
